Since the filename was the only hint about intended content, I assumed it should depict the numeral zero. If you meant something else, tell me what the file should show and I'll redo it.

The file now contains:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="64" height="64" viewBox="0 0 64 64" role="img" aria-labelledby="zero-title">
  <title id="zero-title">Zero</title>
  <ellipse cx="32" cy="32" rx="13" ry="22" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="6"/>
</svg>
```

**What changed**

- **Scalable geometry.** A viewBox plus intrinsic width and height, so the icon scales cleanly at any size and has a default size when used as an image.
- **Accessible name.** A title element wired up with role and aria-labelledby, so screen readers announce it as "Zero".
- **Color inheritance.** The stroke uses currentColor, so the icon follows surrounding text color when inlined and falls back to black standalone.
- **The glyph itself.** A monoline ellipse narrower than it is tall, which reads as a numeral zero rather than a letter O. It sits centered with its stroke fully inside the viewBox.
